executiveSummary: GM0431 identity, Noord-Holland and Veiligheidsregio Zaanstreek-Waterland assignment, full 2025 boundary and CBS resident control are coherent. Fresh context reports 9,733 residents; four published neighbourhood rows sum to 9,730 (-3, -0.031%), a negligible CBS rounding/suppression difference. The bundle preserves Oostzaan plus the De Haal, De Heul and Noordeinde deelkernen, one district, no ProRail station and seven scheduled-transit stop areas. All ten canonical presets execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Oostzaan is a low, subsiding peat-polder and boezem-controlled municipality between Amsterdam and Zaanstad, with Twiske/Oostzanerveld water and recreation geography and concentrated A7/A8/A10/N516 access dependencies. The generic coastal preset applies 1.643007 normalized inundation stress at T+24 to 3,300 residents and leaves 845 affected at T+72 without selecting a defence/breach, boezem/polder or protected-domain case; this value is never 1.64 physical metres. Seven unrelated single hazards reproduce the same complete four-neighbourhood severity order. Exact mobility, care, utility and recovery values exceed the public topology, incident-state, resource and action evidence. Static plans, registers and absent live matches remain context or Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe or operational.

evidenceSources.title: E01 — Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025, table 86165NED, OData API
supports: The official municipality row identifies GM0431 Oostzaan and reports 9,733 residents, density 842 per square kilometre, 22.5% age 65 or older and 1,259 one-person households.

The four published neighbourhood rows sum to 9,730 residents (-3, -0.031%), 4,185 households and 2,190 residents aged 65 or older; deterministic allocation adds three residents to reconcile to the municipal control.
Thirty-four fields cover all four rows, while district-heating share and public-charging counts cover zero rows; null/suppressed values remain Unknown, never official zero.

CBS OData is machine-readable under CC BY 4.0. Annual residents do not establish event-time visitors, patients, pupils, commuters, responders, livestock, shelter occupancy, self-reliance or preparedness.

evidenceSources.publisher: PDOK / CBS / Kadaster / Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi
evidenceSources.title: E02 — Full municipal geometry, settlements and road, rail and scheduled-transit reference inputs
evidenceSources.edition: 2025 boundary/statistics and current generated BAG, BRT, NWB, ProRail and GTFS reference snapshots
supports: The generated centre [4.874886065435427, 52.450048011004725] lies inside the fresh full-resolution 2025 municipal boundary.
The bundle retains one district, four neighbourhoods, BAG place Oostzaan and BRT labels Oostzaan, De Haal, De Heul and Noordeinde; no place-centre exception was reported.
The graph contains five logical boundary edges: A8 to Amsterdam and Zaanstad on one physical corridor, A10 to Amsterdam, and A7/N516 to Zaanstad. It has no ProRail station and seven GTFS stop areas.
The two A8 edges are consecutive series links, never two independent capacity sources; all nominal 260/150 values are scenario ceilings, not observed vehicles per hour or incident throughput.

CBS boundary OGC is half-yearly/CC BY 4.0; BAG is daily/Public Domain Mark 1.0; BRT is CC BY 4.0; NWB monthly and ProRail CC0 1.0. OVapi GTFS is free-use best-effort context without an operational SLA.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Klimaatadaptatie, Molenbuurt water-chain works, concept Mobiliteitsplan and Thorbeckeweg N516 project
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal pages inspected 3 September 2026; Molenbuurt project 2023–2026; concept mobility material from 2025
supports: The municipality explicitly identifies rain-water nuisance, heat stress, rising water, drought and subsidence, and the need to accommodate large precipitation volumes. This is planning context, not an event feed.

The linked Molenbuurt project says Liander renewed electricity cables in 2023, the municipality replaced sewer infrastructure in 2024 and raising/reconstruction began in April 2025. A project record does not establish current completion, redundancy, capacity or incident operation across GM0431.

The concept Mobiliteitsplan is expressly strategic and not a detailed funded implementation programme. The Thorbeckeweg page identifies N516 as a heavily used artery for Oostzaan and Zaanstad areas/business parks, with daily congestion and improvement works.

The inspected municipal pages publish human-readable planning/project context; no stable machine API, complete native stress raster contract, refresh guarantee or explicit analytical reuse licence/NoData schema was found.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Oostzaan/Twiske peil, pumped-drainage and public water-asset context
evidenceSources.edition: Current peilbesluit page; historic Watergebiedsplan De Waterlanden dated 1 June 2013; HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: HHNK publishes current adopted target-level decisions. The older Watergebiedsplan De Waterlanden documents Oostzaan as a pumped drainage area served by gemaal De Waker, with three main peilgebieden, numerous local deviations/underdrainage and hydraulic links to Twiske and Purmerland-West; it is historic mechanism context and must not override current decisions.

The historic plan states Twiske is within the Oostzaan drainage system, can receive water through a closable culvert and returns excess via Twiske Molen. It also notes many small lower-level areas and mobile/wind-pump regulation, demonstrating spatially heterogeneous controls.

The deployment registry assigns 94 points to GM0431: 77 surface-water pumps, sixteen weirs and one sewer pump. The national aggregation is contributor-dependent under CC BY-SA 4.0 and lacks complete topology, comparable capacity, target settings, power/control/backup, maintenance and live operation.
Target levels and registered objects are static context, not achieved incident water levels, available storage, defence condition, pump command, sewer capacity or a flood forecast.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028 and first-72-hour preparedness context
evidenceSources.edition: Risk profile valid from 19 December 2024; national 72-hour guidance current at access
supports: The current regional profile separates primary-defence breach, Markermeer rise affecting buitendijkse areas while the primary defence remains safe, and a local cluster cloudburst. These are illustrative official scenarios, not selected GM0431 incidents.

It identifies extreme rain/drought, dike cracking, heat, nature/berm fire, blocked routes, electricity/telecom/drainage cascades, drinking-water contamination, gas interruption, cyber disruption and care continuity as relevant mechanisms.

A primary-defence breach can inundate a large area within hours and take days to close, while recovery lasts much longer. That example provides no Oostzaan defence segment, breach, footprint, arrival or exercise activation.

National guidance recommends a 72-hour emergency kit including three litres of water per person per day, food, medicine, radio/power and a household plan; it does not measure preparedness, stock or local distribution capacity.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — LIWO flood cases and timestamped weather-warning, water and road screens
supports: LIWO 2025.1.6 contains professional flood-information layers requiring expert water-manager interpretation. A selected case must retain source, defence/breach/control state, protected domain, footprint, native depth/velocity units, arrival/persistence/recession, probability, CRS, licence and NoData.
No Waterinfo observation or forecast point is assigned inside GM0431. Missing point coverage cannot establish current polder/boezem water or defence state and cannot be held through T+72.

The KNMI 48-hour retrieval contains no issued warning record and the NDW current-situation snapshot assigns no valid situation geometry inside GM0431. Those issue-time coverage facts neither validate arbitrary exercise forcing nor prove routes open.

KNMI is CC BY 4.0 and Waterinfo/NDW CC0 unless component terms state otherwise. Operational records require issue, observation, valid and retrieval time, coverage, fault/revision state and an explicit affectsSimulation binding.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Oostzanerveld/Twiske peat landscape, nature, recreation and infrastructure context
evidenceSources.edition: Current provincial area page; provincial landscape guidance and 11 May 2026 Oostzanerveld vision; municipal tourism page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Official provincial material characterizes Oostzanerveld/Twiske as a peat-meadow, water and nature/recreation system where water quality, subsidence, agriculture, nature and recreation interact; the 2026 vision covers 781 hectares and many water-surrounded parcels.

The provincial landscape guidance says historic peat drainage lowered ground to roughly one to two metres below sea level and identifies A7, A8, A10, the Zaandam–Hoorn rail line and high-voltage routes along or through the larger ensemble.

The municipal tourism page describes Twiske as 650 hectares, one-third water, with swimming, diving, surfing, canoeing, sailing, beaches, a harbour, climbing, care-farm and hospitality uses. Oostzanerveld has hundreds of floating-peat islands and water-based access/recreation.

Area and attraction descriptions demonstrate plausible transient presence, water/boat access and eligible vegetation only. They are not live occupancy, visitor counts, ignition/perimeter, fuel moisture, smoke plume, evacuation demand or route capacity; inspected page reuse terms do not state a machine-data licence.

evidenceSources.publisher: Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / KVK-PDOK / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Provider territories, planning/register layers and cross-boundary acute care
evidenceSources.edition: Public-context snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care questionnaire 2026 v1.1
supports: The provider-territory query at Oostzaan's reference point returns Liander for power/gas, PWN for drinking water and Ziggo for telecom, but no drainage provider. The Public Domain provider WMS/WFS is official context and affectsSimulation=false; point membership is not network topology, service state or complete municipal coverage.

One public grid-planning sample maps to Liander OS NOORD PAPAVERWEG 10-1i with 68/74 MW existing/required withdrawal and queues/projects. It is a large-user planning sample, not live load, outage, reserve, feeder topology, switching or restoration.

Municipal screens contain ten RDI antenna installations, six DUO education locations and four KVK-PDOK governmental-service addresses. Registers do not establish coverage, backhaul, people, emergency function, accessibility, stock, backup or operation.

RIVM assigns no emergency department inside GM0431. Zaans Medisch Centrum is about 3.36 km straight-line from the representative centre and reports 24/7 emergency care, acute obstetrics, fifteen treatment rooms and 20,508 visits in 2025; annual CC0 questionnaire data do not establish route time, ambulance availability, acceptance, occupancy, staffing or generator endurance.

No municipal KNMI station/warning, Waterinfo observation/forecast, NDW road situation, RIVM acute-care/PM2.5 or seismic event is assigned. Empty spatial/time matching remains Unknown/NoData, never zero impact or service continuity.
